summary: POC scoping focused on integration planning: SDK usage, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, function/tool calling, and structured output. Discussed success criteria (latency < 300ms p50 for 512 tokens, 95% accuracy on structured extraction tasks), workload sizing (peak 250 RPS simulated, typical 60 RPS), benchmark plan and timeline, and security/compliance needs for a Private/VPC setup.
transcript:
[00:00] Anna Park (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, i'm anna from Redwood, i run the account, we also have liam and priya on the call. quick roll call?
[00:10] Ravi Shah (Equinox AI): hey thanks anna, ravi here, maya and jordan from product are on too.
[00:16] Liam Chen (Redwood SE): hi all, liam, i'll be doing the technical bits, focusing on benchmarks and integration.
[00:22] Jordan Lee (Equinox PM): great, thanks. the goal for today is to scope the poc and make sure we have clear success criteria and timeline.
[00:30] Maya Patel (ML Eng): yes, we're evaluating for a structured extraction feature from support tickets plus a few generate-style assistants. big things are latency and reliability.
[00:40] Anna Park: perfect. to kick off, can you share your current traffic and latency targets?
[00:48] Ravi Shah: so baseline, our service currently sees about 60 rps average, peaks around 250 during spikes, payload size typically 200-600 tokens, target p50 latency under 300 ms for 512 tokens, p95 under 1.2s.
[01:05] Liam Chen: okay that's helpful. for the poc we'll simulate peak using replay traces. we'll need sample traces and your top 3 prompts.
[01:14] Maya Patel: we'll get those. on accuracy, for structured extraction we need field-level F1 > 0.85 on our eval set.
[01:22] Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE): noted, so success criteria: latency + accuracy. also define cost target?
[01:30] Jordan Lee: yes, cost per 1k tokens should be under our current managed endpoint rate, otherwise it'll be hard to justify.
[01:37] Anna Park: ok we'll include unit-cost estimates in the proposal.
[01:42] [00:45] Liam Chen: quick architecture note - you can integrate via our OpenAI-compatible http endpoint or our SDKs (python/node/go). for fast test we recommend the OpenAI-compatible endpoint so you can reuse existing client code.
[01:55] Maya Patel: important - does function/tool calling work over the OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or only via SDKs? we heavily rely on tool calls to hit our internal search and db.
[02:06] Liam Chen: function calling is supported on the OpenAI-compatible endpoints, though some advanced features (like streaming structured output + tool metadata) are smoother via our SDK which handles retries and kv cache preservation. note our transcription/transcript: meaning, sorry, our runtime also preserves KV cache across bursts to reduce cost.
[02:25] Ravi Shah: kv cash?
[02:27] Priya Kapoor: kv cache, sorry the auto transcribed had a small swap.
[02:30] Jordan Lee: for structured output we want strict JSON schema enforcement. how does Redwood support that?
[02:35] Liam Chen: we have structured-output helpers in the SDK which map model outputs to a schema and do a post-parse verify; we can also run an eval harness that checks generation conformity across prompts. the OpenAI-compatible way is to use function responses with specified parameter schemas - that works too but SDK gives extra instrumentation.
[02:50] Maya Patel: ok good. security: we need SOC2 + SSO (SAML) and optional VPC/private deployment. what are timelines for Private?
[03:00] Anna Park: we have a Private offering with a customer-managed control plane, typical on-prem/VPC engagements start with a scoping call then 6-8 week delivery for a minimal private stack, depending on customer infra. for the poc we usually start on Hosted with dedicated capacity or a VPC-linked trial.
[03:18] Ravi Shah: and KMS integration for keys? we require customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest.
[03:24] Priya Kapoor: yes KMS/HSM can be integrated; we'll share the security docs and audit checklist - SOC2/ISO items are included.
[03:33] Jordan Lee: bench plan and timeline?
[03:36] Liam Chen: propose week 1 we set up trial tenant + ingestion of sample traces; week 2 run synthetic replay and basic correctness evals; week 3 run scaled benchmarks for peak rps and latency SLOs, week 4 iterate and tune batching/quantization to hit cost/latency goals. overall 4 weeks to a POC report if artifacts and access are provided quickly.
[03:58] Maya Patel: that fits our timeline, target internal sign-off by mid-May.
[04:05] Anna Park: excellent. a couple of gotchas - if you use the OpenAI-compatible endpoint and later move to Private deployment, some endpoint names change; we'll provide a migration guide. also note model variants: we can route to lower-cost quantized variants if accuracy allows.
[04:22] Ravi Shah: competitors question - do you do on-prem benchmarking with Anthropic/OPenAI models to compare? we want apples-to-apples.
[04:31] Liam Chen: yes we can run comparative benchmarks, though licensing for some closed models requires separate entitlements; OpenAI-compatible tests are straightforward for open models and self-hosted variants.
[04:42] Jordan Lee: for integration: what about streaming responses and partial structured output? we may stream incremental fields as they arrive.
[04:50] Priya Kapoor: streaming structured output is supported; SDKs expose an evented parser that emits partial JSON and finalization events, but if you need absolute atomic json per response we can enforce that in the eval harness.
[05:02] Maya Patel: great. for the POC can we run a smaller internal benchmark first to validate accuracy before we spin up the larger load test?
[05:09] Liam Chen: absolutely, that's our recommended flow - correctness first, then scale. we'll provide the harness and config.
[05:15] Anna Park: i'll send the POC proposal with success criteria (latency p50<300ms, p95<1.2s, structured F1>0.85), scope, timeline, and pricing.
[05:26] Ravi Shah: and please include the SDK quickstart and the OpenAI-compatible endpoint example, plus notes on function calling and structured outputs.
[05:34] Liam Chen: will do, i'll attach example code for python and node.
[05:38] [05:40] Jordan Lee: next steps?
[05:42] Anna Park: recap - anna sends proposal, liam shares SDK + harness, maya uploads prompts/traces, schedule tech deep dive next week.
[05:50] Maya Patel: yep that works. thanks everyone.
[05:53] Anna Park: thanks all, we'll follow up via email with links.
[05:58] [END]
